newsitem.title: FINLAND: Rautaruukki upbeat on 97, silent on float.
newsitem.headline: Rautaruukki upbeat on 97, silent on float.

text.p: Finnish state-controlled steel group Rautaruukki Oy's CEO Mikko Kivimaki on Wednesday declined comment on a potential further privatisation of the company, but said steel prices could rise this year.
"The fall in (steel) prices came to a halt last autumn, and in some steel grades they have turned higher ... and conditions exist for a positive price trend," Kivimaki told Reuters by telephone.
"This year is likely to be a mirror image of 1996, when prices were high at the beginning of the year, but then fell," he said, adding production volumes have remained high.

Kivimaki declined comment on an announcement late on Tuesday by the Finnish ministry of trade and industry, which said it had appointed investment banks SBC Warburg and UBS as advisers for a review of possibilities to broaden the ownership base of Rautaruukki.
"It is an owner's task to investigate such things," Kivimaki said.
The ministry said no decision had been made to further privatise Rautaruukki.
The Finnish state holds 68.7 percent of votes in Rautaruukki, and has an authorisation by parliament to cut the state's holding to 33.4 percent.
